vedic_reference.note: Vishwajit is a name found in the Rigveda and is associated with the god Indra, who is often depicted as the god of victory. The name Vishwajeet is derived from this ancient Indian tradition, symbolizing the victorious son of the universe.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Vishwajeet" carries a grand and regal connotation in Hindu culture. It implies an individual of immense power, strength, and victoriousness. In ancient India, titles like Vishwajeet were bestowed upon great kings and rulers to acknowledge their conquest and domination over a vast territory. Similarly, Vishwajeet was also a revered title for gods and deities, representing their supreme power and rule over the entire universe.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Vishwajeet" signifies overcoming personal limitations and expanding one's consciousness beyond the self. The deep inner meaning of the name encourages the pursuit of spiritual growth, wisdom, and ultimately, the conquest of one's inner self. It invokes the spirit of dedicating ourselves towards the ultimate goal of realizing our true potential and fulfilling our divine purpose.

historical_references.reference: The name Vishwajeet was given to Shivaji, the founder of the Maratha Empire in western India. He was crowned in 1674 and his reign lasted until his death in 1680. The name Vishwajeet translates to 'conqueror of the universe'.

Vishwajeet is also the name of a Hindu deity, Vishwajeet Vishnu, who is considered the god of victory and success. According to Hindu mythology, Vishwajeet Vishnu is the preserver god and one of the primary deities in the Hindu pantheon.
